title: What training does FAA Part 121 require for airline crewmembers and dispatchers?
description: What 14 CFR Part 121 Subpart N requires of airline training programs: FAA approval, initial and 12 month recurrent training, and Part 5 SMS training.
shortAnswer: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requires every Part 121 air carrier to run an FAA approved training program under 14 CFR Part 121 Subpart N that adequately trains each crewmember, aircraft dispatcher, flight instructor and check pilot. Crewmembers need initial training for their airplane type and position, then recurrent training within the preceding 12 calendar months, with an extra 6 month recurrent flight requirement for captains. Under 14 CFR 5.91, carriers must also train staff in their safety management system.
keyTakeaways: Under 14 CFR 121.401, each certificate holder must establish a training program meeting Subpart N and Appendices E and F, and must obtain initial and final FAA approval before implementing it.

Under 14 CFR 121.433, no one may serve as a required crewmember without initial training for the type and position, and recurrent training plus any required check within the preceding 12 calendar months; pilots in command also need recurrent flight training within 6 calendar months.
Recurrent ground training has programmed hour minimums in 121.427, such as 24 hours for Group II (turbojet) pilots and 12 hours for Group II flight attendants, unless reduced by the FAA.
Certain emergency drills under 121.417 are required in initial training and once each 24 calendar months, and captains need leadership, command and mentoring training within 36 months.
14 CFR 5.91 requires Part 121 carriers to train the accountable executive, managers and employees to attain and maintain the competencies needed for their SMS duties.
appliesTo: Air carriers certificated under 14 CFR Part 119 to conduct domestic, flag or supplemental operations under Part 121
Pilots, flight engineers and flight attendants serving as required crewmembers
Aircraft dispatchers in domestic and flag operations
Flight instructors, check pilots, check flight engineers and SMS accountable executives and managers

sections.heading: What must a Part 121 training program include?

blocks.text: A Part 121 carrier must have an FAA approved training program that ensures each crewmember, aircraft dispatcher, flight instructor, check pilot and check flight engineer is adequately trained for their assigned duties. [14 CFR 121.401(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.401) also requires adequate ground and flight training facilities, properly qualified ground instructors, current training material for each airplane type, and enough instructors and check pilots to deliver the training and checks.

Approval is a two stage process: "Prior to implementation, the certificate holder must obtain initial and final FAA approval of the training program." Each instructor, supervisor or check pilot responsible for a training segment or check must certify the person's proficiency and knowledge on completion, and that certification becomes part of the crewmember's or dispatcher's record.

Subpart N defines the categories of training in [14 CFR 121.400](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.400): initial, transition, upgrade, conversion, differences, requalification and related aircraft differences training. Airplanes are grouped as Group I (propeller driven, reciprocating or turbopropeller) and Group II (turbojet), and programmed hour minimums differ by group. Carriers may alternatively qualify crews through an Advanced Qualification Program under Subpart Y, which this page does not cover in detail.

sections.heading: What initial training must crewmembers complete?

blocks.text: Before serving as a required crewmember, a person must complete initial ground and flight training for that airplane type and crewmember position in an approved program, unless transition, upgrade or conversion training applies. This rule is in [14 CFR 121.433(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.433).

Ground training content is set by [14 CFR 121.415](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.415). Newly hired crewmembers and dispatchers receive basic indoctrination ground training of 40 programmed hours unless reduced, covering crewmember duties, applicable Federal Aviation Regulations, the operating certificate and operations specifications (not required for flight attendants), and the carrier's operating manual. Position specific ground training, emergency training under 121.417 and 121.805, and training on the carrier's passenger recovery plan where applicable follow.

Where a carrier's program includes differences training for a variant of an airplane, no one may serve on that variant without completing initial, transition or differences training for it (121.433(b)).

sections.heading: How often is recurrent training required?

blocks.text: Every 12 calendar months, with an additional 6 month requirement for pilots in command. Under 14 CFR 121.433(c), no one may serve as a required crewmember unless, within the preceding 12 calendar months, flight crewmembers have completed recurrent ground and flight training and any applicable flight check, and flight attendants and dispatchers have completed recurrent ground training and a competence check.

Pilots in command must also have completed, within the preceding 6 calendar months, recurrent flight training in an airplane in which they serve as captain. A proficiency check under 121.441 may substitute for recurrent flight training, but not for extended envelope training or low-altitude windshear training. Under 121.401(b), training or a check completed in the calendar month before or after the due month counts as completed in the due month.

[14 CFR 121.427](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.427) sets the content. Recurrent ground training must include a quiz or other review of knowledge, instruction as needed in the position's ground subjects, competence checks for flight attendants and dispatchers, and crew resource management (CRM) or dispatch resource management (DRM) training. Pilots serving as pilot in command must also complete recurrent ground training on leadership and command and mentoring within 36 months preceding that service.

blocks.text: Pilot recurrent programmed hours must include 30 additional minutes for extended envelope training (121.427(f)). Separately, [14 CFR 121.417](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.417) requires certain additional emergency drills during initial training and "once each 24 calendar months during recurrent training".

sections.heading: What SMS training does 14 CFR Part 5 require of Part 121 carriers?

blocks.text: Part 121 carriers must train the people accountable for safety so they can perform their SMS duties. [14 CFR 5.91](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-5.91) states that any person required to have an SMS "must provide training to each individual identified in § 5.23 of this part to ensure the individuals attain and maintain the competencies necessary to perform their duties relevant to the operation and performance of the SMS."

The individuals identified in [14 CFR 5.23](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-5.23) are the accountable executive, all members of management for SMS processes in their area (hazard identification and risk assessment, assuring risk control effectiveness, safety promotion, advising the accountable executive), and employees relative to safety performance. Section 5.93 adds safety communication duties, including making employees aware of SMS policies, processes and tools relevant to their responsibilities and explaining why safety procedures are introduced or changed.

Part 5 sets no hours or interval for this training; the standard is attaining and maintaining competence. The FAA's [April 26, 2024 final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/26/2024-08669/safety-management-systems) amended Part 5 and extended it beyond Part 121. Under 14 CFR 5.7, Part 121 carriers with an SMS accepted on or before May 28, 2024 had to revise it to meet the amended Part by May 28, 2025. Part 135 operators and section 91.147 Letter of Authorization holders must implement an SMS by May 28, 2027 (14 CFR 5.9), which matters for groups operating under both Parts.

sections.heading: How can carriers map Part 121 training obligations to evidence?

blocks.text: Subpart N and Part 5 obligations recur on different clocks: on hire, every 6 or 12 calendar months, every 24 or 36 months, or only when competence needs maintaining. The summary below groups them by position with the record an FAA inspector would look for under [14 CFR 121.683](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-121.683), which requires records of training, checks and qualifications.

blocks.text: Calendar month grace rules make interval tracking error prone, so carriers usually compute due dates in the records system rather than by hand. The approach in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) and [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) applies directly.

sections.heading: What other training rules apply to Part 121 carriers?

blocks.text: Subpart N is the core, but several other rules sit beside it. Hazardous materials training under Subpart Z must be completed within the past 24 months for anyone performing hazmat job functions; see [air dangerous goods training requirements](/regulations/iata-dangerous-goods-training-requirements). Supervisors who make reasonable cause or reasonable suspicion drug and alcohol testing decisions need training under 14 CFR Part 120, described in [DOT drug and alcohol supervisor training](/regulations/dot-drug-and-alcohol-supervisor-training).

As at November 2026, the most recent amendments to 121.401, 121.427 and 121.433 shown in the eCFR date from a June 18, 2024 rule. Training managers should check the eCFR and FAA notices before each annual curriculum review.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures each Subpart N curriculum segment and each Part 5 SMS role as defined competencies with assessment points, so that the quiz, competence check or flight check tied to a recurrent cycle can be traced to what it tests. When a regulation, operations specification or airplane variant changes, the affected segments and crewmember records can be identified directly.

faqs.q: Is recurrent training due every 12 months or every calendar year?
faqs.a: Every 12 calendar months. Section 121.433(c) requires completion within the preceding 12 calendar months, and section 121.401(b) treats training or checks completed in the calendar month before or after the due month as completed in the due month, which gives a three month window without shifting the anniversary.

faqs.q: Can recurrent ground training hours be reduced?
faqs.a: Yes. The programmed hours in 121.427(c) apply unless reduced under 121.405, which allows the FAA to approve a lesser amount where the certificate holder shows circumstances justify it. Content requirements, such as the knowledge review and CRM or DRM training, still apply.

faqs.q: Does Part 5 require a specific SMS course for every employee?
faqs.a: No specific course or hours are prescribed. Section 5.91 requires training that ensures the accountable executive, managers and employees identified under 5.23 attain and maintain the competencies needed for their SMS duties, so content and depth should differ by role.

faqs.q: What happens if a crewmember misses recurrent training?
faqs.a: They may not serve as a required crewmember until requalified. Section 121.400 defines requalification training as training for crewmembers previously trained and qualified who have become unqualified by not meeting the recurrent training or proficiency check requirements within the required period.
